$comment: Positive half of the tct-011/tct-012 pair. `ext.com.example.debug_trace` is a vendor-namespaced key (registries/extension-keys.md naming rules; RFC-AITP-0012 §1.1 applies the same reverse-domain guidance to `ext` as to `extensions`) that is NOT in the extension-key registry — deliberately unrecognized. `ext` itself is a schema-defined optional claim (`aitp-tct.schema.json` properties.ext) covered by the JWS signature over the payload segment like any other claim, so it is schema-permitted rather than exempt from signing.
description: TCT decoded claims carry an unrecognized, vendor-namespaced key (`ext.com.example.debug_trace`) INSIDE the OPTIONAL `ext` claim. RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.5/§7 and RFC-AITP-0012 §1.1/§5: unknown keys inside `ext` MUST be ignored and MUST NOT drive a trust decision, but `ext` itself remains a schema-permitted, ordinary part of the signed claims. The receiver accepts: claims are otherwise identical in shape to tct-011's unaffected-by-expiry claims, and the unrecognized nested key does not affect TCT verification (audience, expiry, signature all otherwise pass). Counterpart: tct-011, where the same kind of unrecognized claim placed OUTSIDE `ext` is rejected with UNKNOWN_FIELD.

expected.rationale: TCT signature verifies over the JWS payload segment INCLUDING `ext`; audience matches the verifying peer, and `exp` is far in the future. The unrecognized `ext.com.example.debug_trace` key is ignored for trust-decision purposes per RFC-AITP-0001 §7 and RFC-AITP-0012 §1.1/§5, but remains part of the signed bytes and MUST NOT be treated as an unpermitted claim.
